verified.story_title: House GOP blocks FY2027 NDAA procedural vote June 30, stalling Sullivan's $2.6B Alaska package
verified.usable_facts: On June 30, 2026 House Republicans (a 198-224 rule vote) failed to bring the FY2027 NDAA to the floor, canceling the week before the July 4 recess. The broader NDAA carries Sen. Sullivan's 56 provisions and $2.6 billion in Alaska authorizations, incl. $15M resilient autonomous Arctic sensing and $10M autonomy within Golden Dome. Committee-advanced AUTHORIZATION, not appropriated.
verified.industry_consequence: Alaska defense contractors and technology vendors at JBER, Eielson, Fort Wainwright face continued authorization uncertainty on the $2.6B FY2027 package incl. autonomy/Arctic sensing; timeline unclear past early July.
verified.writer_guidance: Attribute $2.6B / provisions to Sullivan's office; call it committee-advanced authorization NOT appropriated. Frame the June 30 failure as the HOUSE rule vote stalling the broader NDAA; do not assert Sullivan's Senate provisions were themselves voted down.

verified.story_title: Alaska LNG tax bill (HB 381) misses July 1 target; conference to July 16, session expires July 19
verified.usable_facts: Conference committee on HB 381 (the tax-relief package Glenfarne says is essential to the Alaska LNG pipeline, project cost estimated at $55 billion per ADN) failed to finish by its informal July 1 target; lawmakers back July 16, special session expires July 19. Glenfarne President Adam Prestidge objected to a Senate amendment adding prevailing-wage/apprenticeship mandates beyond the June 11 union MOU; a proposed corporate income tax on private developers that Dunleavy has said he'd veto is the other open issue.
verified.industry_consequence: Every Railbelt/North Slope large-load data-center case is premised on affordable North Slope gas via the pipeline; a delayed or dead bill raises power-cost forecasts for any AI compute operator. Glenfarne/AGDC face a July 19 cliff.
verified.writer_guidance: Use $55 billion (ADN) NOT $44B, or hedge 'tens of billions'. Keep Glenfarne, Adam Prestidge, July 16 return, July 19 expiry. Corporate income tax = Dunleavy veto threat.

verified.story_title: DAF AI data-center lease RFLP (AFCEC-26-R-0006) closed June 29 at JBER, Eielson, Clear SFS; evaluation begins
verified.usable_facts: AFICA's RFLP for commercial AI data centers across JBER, Eielson, Clear SFS hit its amended June 29, 2026 deadline and moved to evaluation, no award as of July 1. Best-value lease; selected partners would self-finance, build, operate.
verified.industry_consequence: Railbelt utilities (Chugach Electric, GVEA) and broadband providers face a step-change in industrial load requests once a lessee is named; would be Alaska's first large-scale private AI compute campuses on federal land.
verified.writer_guidance: Keep AFCEC-26-R-0006, June 29, three named installations, 'no award yet / evaluation phase'. Safe to note ~4,700 acres / multiple parcels per Air & Space Forces if useful.

verified.story_title: Air Force Under Secretary Lohmeier tours JBER and Eielson, signals ~$8B Alaska investment over five years
verified.usable_facts: USecAF Matthew Lohmeier visited JBER and Eielson June 22-24, called Alaska 'the crossroads of the Arctic and the Pacific' (quote confirmed verbatim in ExecutiveGov), pointed to roughly $8 billion in Air Force investment over five years. Visit coincided with the final week of the RFLP window that closed June 29.
verified.industry_consequence: Most explicit senior Air Force endorsement yet of Alaska as a multi-year federal capital destination; utilities/contractors seeking site-prep or power roles must engage the contracting office during evaluation.
verified.writer_guidance: JBER.mil primary 403'd; survives on ExecutiveGov which confirms both the quote and 'about $8 billion over five years'. Attribute figure to Air Force officials / the Under Secretary, phrase as 'about $8 billion'. Quote 'crossroads of the Arctic and the Pacific' is safe verbatim.

verified.story_title: Dunleavy vetoes ~$16M in pipeline and vocational workforce training from FY2027 budget (June 24)
verified.usable_facts: Dunleavy signed the FY2027 budget June 24 while vetoing about $89.5M total, including roughly $16M across workforce-training facilities (AVTEC ~$5.3M, Alaska Teamsters construction driver training ~$5.2M, Fairbanks Pipeline Training Center ~$4M per ADN itemization). Senate Finance co-chair Bert Stedman said 'We're trying to push forward for a gas line' (verbatim confirmed in Alaska Public Media).
verified.industry_consequence: AVTEC, Fairbanks Pipeline Training Center, Teamsters training lose expansion funding, shrinking the in-state credentialed labor pool for pipeline preconstruction the same week the LNG tax bill stalled.
verified.writer_guidance: $89.5M total is safe. Use 'roughly $16 million' for the workforce grouping (Alaska Public Media). Stedman quote 'We're trying to push forward for a gas line' is safe verbatim if attributed. Named facilities safe.

verified.story_title: Alaska AI-generated CSAM ban takes effect July 1 as part of omnibus crime package
verified.usable_facts: A new Alaska law banning creation/possession of AI-generated child sexual abuse material took effect July 1, 2026, part of an omnibus crime package sponsored by Rep. Sarah Vance; creates state felony charges independent of federal law. Confirmed in ADN.
verified.industry_consequence: Alaska-operating AI developers/platforms face new state criminal exposure effective July 1. Editorial use: the one AI decision that actually took effect this week.
verified.writer_guidance: Single-sourced but primary-adjacent (public law). Use as the contrast/kicker device (the only AI thing that landed), not a load-bearing economic claim. Keep Rep. Sarah Vance, July 1.

verified.story_title: Alaska DNR extends STAK Energy North Slope data-center lease comment period to July 17
verified.usable_facts: Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas posted an updated notice extending the comment deadline on its preliminary best-interest finding for STAK Energy's proposed gas-powered HPC campus (715.4 acres, ~26 mi south of Deadhorse, accessed via Dalton Highway corridor) from June 15 to July 17, 2026; extension reflects public interest not new applicant info; preliminary decision toward a 50-year lease unchanged.
verified.industry_consequence: STAK's path to final lease execution now runs at least through late July, another buildout clock that slipped this week.
verified.writer_guidance: Keep STAK Energy, North Slope / Dalton Highway, comment period extended to July 17, 50-year lease preliminary. Good as a 'slipped clock' texture item.

verified.story_title: Alaska RHTP $272M application cycle closed June 22; AI-enabled healthcare grants expected Aug 1
verified.usable_facts: Alaska's application portal for the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program closed June 22 after advancing 400+ projects; implementation grants expected Aug 1, 2026. AI-enabled tools and drone-supported delivery are eligible categories (GovTech). $272M is the Year 1 CMS allocation per GovTech (Alaska Public says >$1B over five years). Rep. Genevieve Mina said the design is 'almost directing us to AI' (GovTech). Applicants incl. Tanana Chiefs Conference (drone delivery) and Providence.
verified.industry_consequence: Aug 1 is the next real Alaska AI-capital date: the state names implementation-grant awardees from the ~$272M Year-1 pool.
verified.writer_guidance: Background/forward-look. Attribute '$272M Year 1' to GovTech/CMS; do NOT say 'largest in Alaska history'. Aug 1 grant date is the forward hook. Mina quote safe verbatim if attributed.

verified.story_title: Alaska minimum wage rises to $14/hr July 1 (Ballot Measure 1)
verified.usable_facts: Alaska minimum wage rose to $14/hr effective July 1, 2026 (Ballot Measure 1), confirmed via ADN July-1-laws article. The $1,120/week exempt salary threshold and the Dan Robinson quote could NOT be verified (Alaska Beacon 403, DOLWD URL was the wrong release).
verified.industry_consequence: Weak/optional. $14/hr floor for AK employers effective July 1.
verified.writer_guidance: OPTIONAL/likely cut. If used, ONLY the $14/hr July 1 fact (ADN-confirmed). DROP the $1,120 exempt threshold and the Dan Robinson quote entirely (unverified).

verified.story_title: Workforce Pell Grants launch July 1; only 12 states had published eligibility frameworks
verified.usable_facts: Federal Workforce Pell Grant program opened July 1, 2026 for short-term certificate programs; per KMXT/NPR only 12 states had published eligible-program frameworks. The specific claim that Alaska/UA is locked out could NOT be verified from cited sources (neither names Alaska or UA).
verified.industry_consequence: Weak/optional. National launch; states without frameworks can't disburse yet.
verified.writer_guidance: OPTIONAL/likely cut. Do NOT assert 'Alaska/UA locked out' (unverified). If touched at all, only the national fact: Workforce Pell opened July 1, only 12 states had frameworks published.
